newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Movement remains slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Movement remains slow.

text.p: Farmer sales of spring wheat were at a very slow pace on Tuesday following a drop in prices while some producers remained preoccupied finishing off planting, grain dealers said.

They noted USDA reported that 83 percent of the U.S. spring wheat crop was planted as of Sunday, unchanged from the five-year average but above last year's 65 percent at the same stage. "It was towards the high end of expectations," one dealer said.
Heavy rains in Montana over the long holiday weekend largely alleviated concern about dry weather in the state.
"We needed it," one Montana dealer said.
In the Red River Valley farmers were beginning to get back in the fields on Tuesday after rains last Thursday brought seeding to a virtual halt.
Dealers noted the recent drop in prices had helped to reduce farmer selling interest. July MGE futures closed 12-1/4 cents lower at $3.81-3/4 a bushel.
